newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says to check Australia anthrax outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Manila says to check Australia anthrax outbreak.

text.p: The Philippines will verify reports on the outbreak of anthrax in dairy herds in Australia to determine if it will affect the country's import of live animals, dairy products and meat from that country, a government official said on Wednesday.

"We will ask the Australian embassy to supply us information on how extensive the outbreak is," Victor Atienza, head of the animal health division of the Philippine Bureau of Animal Industry told Reuters in an interview.
"But I don't think the Australian Quarantine and Inspection Service will issue health certificates on Australian dairy and meat products if these were infected," Atienza said.
The Philippines has been importing more than 100,000 feeder cattle from Australia annually since 1989, he said. The animals are fattened locally before they are slaughtered.
Atienza said the animals come mostly from Australia's Northern Territories.
In Australia, dairy industry and government officials said early today 68 animals were killed on about 31 farms in the state of Victoria.
Anthrax, a bacterial infection, causes rapid death in cattle, sheep and goats which eat contaminated material. It rarely affected humans but can be contracted through a small cut or scratch.
